paragraphs: In this Annual Report on Form 10-K, "we," "our," "us," "Annexon" and the "Company" refer to Annexon, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiary. Annexon, Annexon, Inc., the Annexon logo and other trade names, trademarks or service marks of Annexon are the property of Annexon, Inc. This report contains references to our trademarks and to trademarks belonging to other entities. Trade names, trademarks and service marks of other companies appearing in this report are the property of their respective holders. We do not intend our use or display of other companies' trade names or trademarks to imply a relationship with, or endorsement or sponsorship of us by, any other companies.

We are a biopharmaceutical company advancing the next generation platform of targeted immunotherapies aimed at complement-mediated neuroinflammatory diseases that impact nearly 10 million people worldwide. The classical complement pathway is a core component to the body's immune system that activates a powerful inflammatory cascade. We believe that by stopping the classical complement pathway at its start by targeting C1q, the initiating molecule of the classical complement pathway, our approach may have the potential to provide more complete protection against complement-mediated disorders of the body, brain and eye.

Using our proprietary platform, we are identifying and characterizing the role of the classical complement pathway in three therapeutic areas—autoimmune, neurodegeneration and ophthalmology. In so doing, we are advancing a pipeline of product candidates designed to block the early classical cascade and all downstream pathway components and their tissue-damaging functions. Our goal is to suppress excessive or aberrant classical complement activity that contributes to chronic inflammation and tissue damage to slow or even halt disease progression, while preserving the beneficial immune functions of the lectin and alternative complement pathways involved in the clearance of pathogens and damaged cells. Building on more than a decade of expertise stopping acute and chronic neuroinflammation at its source, we have demonstrated robust target engagement in the body, brain and eye, and clinical proof of concept in multiple diseases.

Our strategic priorities include advancing two late-stage registrational programs: tanruprubart, toward our first potential approval in Guillain-Barré Syndrome, or GBS, and vonaprument, toward pivotal data in geographic atrophy, or GA, as well as developing ANX1502, a novel oral small molecule for autoimmune conditions.

Tanruprubart is an investigational targeted immunotherapy delivered in a single infusion to rapidly halt aggressive neuroinflammation and damage in GBS, an acute, rare, neuromuscular emergency that annually affects ~150,000 people worldwide. There are currently no therapies approved by the FDA for GBS and no substantial evidence of effectiveness from the current standard of care. In the placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial, approximately 90% of GBS patients treated with tanruprubart improved by week 1 and more than twice as many treated patients achieved a normal state of health at week 26. Tanruprubart has consistently demonstrated rapid and sustained functional improvements across a comprehensive data package that includes successful placebo-controlled proof-of-concept, or POC, and Phase 3 data, Real-World Evidence, or RWE, indirect comparison data of tanruprubart's treatment effect versus current standard of care, and drug-drug interaction safety data with tanruprubart with current standard of care. Completed placebo-controlled studies were conducted in Southeast Asia given GBS' sudden and debilitating disease course and lack of approved comparator in the U.S. The open-label FORWARD study in the U.S. and Europe is ongoing and designed to support a broad intended label for the treatment of GBS and further expand the use of tanruprubart across geographies.

We filed the Marketing Authorization Application, or MAA, with the European Medicines Agency, or EMA, for tanruprubart for the treatment of GBS in January 2026, and we continue to engage with EU regulators through the MAA review process. Tanruprubart has been granted orphan designation from the EMA. Tanruprubart has also been granted Fast Track and orphan drug designation for the treatment of GBS from the FDA. The currently ongoing open-label U.S./EU FORWARD study is designed to broaden Western experience with tanruprubart, and we anticipate initial pharmacokinetics, or PK, pharmacodynamics, or PD, biomarker and functional data in 2026 to supplement our comprehensive data package for tanruprubart in GBS. Following such data, we plan to engage with the FDA with the

goal of reaching alignment on our current and supplemental data package and information supporting the generalizability of tanruprubart in Western patients for submission of a biologics license application, or BLA, in 2026.

Vonaprument is an investigational neuroprotective inhibitor of C1q and the classical complement cascade delivered intravitreally for dry AMD with GA, a leading cause of blindness affecting more than eight million people worldwide. There are no approved therapies for GA targeting the preservation of vision. Vonaprument is the only investigational therapy in GA to show significant vision preservation on assessments of best corrected visual acuity, or BCVA, and low luminance visual acuity, or LLVA, demonstrating significant protection from vision loss in both normal and low light conditions, as well as significant preservation of central retinal photoreceptors necessary for visual acuity. In the Phase 2 ARCHER trial, vonaprument also reduced risk of 15-letter vision loss by more than 70%.

In July 2025, we completed enrollment of 659 patients in ARCHER II, a global, sham-controlled, double-masked Phase 3 trial for patients with GA. The primary endpoint of ARCHER II is the gold standard for visual acuity, measuring proportion of patients with confirmed BCVA ≥15-letter loss at any two consecutive visits through month 15. A secondary endpoint is ellipsoid zone, or EZ, loss, which is a key anatomic measure of photoreceptor health and function. We plan to report topline data in the fourth quarter of 2026.

We have established a global registration path with the FDA and EMA, which supports the potential of vonaprument to be the first treatment approved in both Europe and the U.S. for the protection of vision in patients with GA. The single-study program will be analyzed as two sub-studies in the U.S. in accordance with the FDA's two-trial recommendation. Vonaprument is the first and only therapeutic candidate for the treatment of GA to receive Priority Medicine, or PRIME, designation by the EMA, which provides early and proactive support to developers of promising medicines that may offer a major therapeutic advantage over existing treatments or benefit to patients without treatment options. Vonaprument was also selected by the EMA for the Product Development Coordinator Pilot launched in July 2025 to help PRIME designation holders efficiently navigate regulatory interactions including expedited scientific advice, MAA submission readiness activities, and ad-hoc queries throughout the development program.

ANX1502 is a novel oral small molecule inhibiting the activated form of C1s, an enzyme carried by C1q to initiate the classical cascade, which we believe is first-in-kind and has the potential to offer the advantages of selective upstream classical complement inhibition with the convenience and flexibility of oral administration. In a Phase 1 single-ascending dose, or SAD, and multiple-ascending dose, or MAD, clinical trial in healthy volunteers designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, PK and PD, ANX1502 was generally well tolerated across cohorts with no serious adverse events, achieved target levels of active drug and showed supportive impact on a PD biomarker of complement activity. We are evaluating an enteric-coated tablet formulation of ANX1502 in an ongoing POC study in patients with cold agglutinin disease, or CAD. We have observed drug levels at and exceeding the pre-defined target in fasted CAD patients. Dosing is ongoing to enhance our understanding of ANX1502's profile and we plan to provide an update upon study completion in 2026.

Annexon was co-founded by the late Dr. Ben Barres, former member of the National Academy of Sciences, Chair of Neurobiology at Stanford University and a pioneer in complement-mediated neurodegeneration, and Dr. Arnon Rosenthal, a world-renowned scientist and industry executive. We have assembled a seasoned and accomplished management team that has been involved in the discovery, development, approval and commercialization of numerous marketed drugs, and has been studying the complement pathway and autoimmune and neurodegenerative disorders for decades. Our team is further supported by an experienced scientific advisory board, board of directors and leading healthcare investors that share our commitment to developing disease-modifying medicines for patients with neuroinflammatory diseases of the body, brain and eye.

We hold worldwide development and commercialization rights, including through exclusive licenses, to all of our product candidates, which allows us to strategically maximize value from our product portfolio over time. Our patent portfolio includes patent protection for our targeted immunotherapy platform and each of our product candidates.

headings: Risks Related to Our Limited Operating History, Financial Condition and Capital Requirements
Our results of operations may fluctuate significantly, which makes our future results of operations difficult to predict and could cause our results of operations to fall below expectations.
Our business is heavily dependent on the successful development, regulatory approval and commercialization of our product candidates, some of which are in early stages of clinical development.

Public health crises such as pandemics or similar outbreaks have, and could in the future, materially and adversely affect our preclinical and clinical trials, business, financial condition and results of operations.
We may encounter substantial delays in our clinical trials or may not be able to conduct or complete our clinical trials on the timelines we expect, if at all.
If we encounter difficulties enrolling patients in our clinical trials, our clinical development activities could be delayed or otherwise adversely affected.
Even if our current or future product candidates obtain regulatory approval, they may fail to achieve the broad degree of physician and patient adoption and use necessary for commercial success.

paragraphs: Our business involves significant risks, some of which are described below. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below, together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and the financial statements and the related notes. If any of the following risks actually occur, it could harm our business, prospects, results of operations and financial condition and future prospects. In such event, the market price of our common stock could decline and you could lose all or part of your investment. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial may also impair our business operations. This Annual Report on Form 10-K also contains forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of factors that are described below and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K.

We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company with a limited operating history and no products approved for commercial sale. We have incurred significant losses since our inception, and we anticipate that we will continue to incur significant losses for the foreseeable future, which, together with our limited operating history, makes it difficult to assess our future viability.

We are a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company, and we have only a limited operating history upon which you can evaluate our business and prospects. Biopharmaceutical product development is a highly speculative undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk. We have no products approved for commercial sale and have not generated any revenue from sales of our product candidates and have incurred losses in each year since our inception in March 2011. We have only a limited operating history upon which you can evaluate our business and prospects. In addition, we have not yet demonstrated an ability to successfully overcome many of the risks and uncertainties frequently encountered by companies in new and rapidly evolving fields, particularly in the pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical and biotechnology industry.

We have had significant operating losses since our inception. Our net loss for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 was approximately $206.7 million and $138.2 million, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $917.4 million. Substantially all of our losses have resulted from expenses incurred in connection with our research and development programs and from general and administrative costs associated with our operations. We expect to continue to incur losses for the foreseeable future, and we anticipate these losses will continue as we develop our product candidates, conduct clinical trials and pursue research and development activities. Even if we achieve profitability in the future, we may not be able to sustain profitability in subsequent periods. Our prior losses, combined with expected future losses, have had and will continue to have an adverse effect on our stockholders' equity and working capital.

We will require substantial additional financing to achieve our goals, and a failure to obtain this necessary capital when needed on acceptable terms, or at all, could force us to delay, limit, reduce or terminate our product development programs, commercialization efforts or other operations.

Since our inception, we have invested a significant portion of our efforts and financial resources in research and development activities. Our product candidates will require additional clinical development, and we intend to conduct additional research and development activities to discover and develop new product candidates, including conducting preclinical studies and clinical trials, all of which will require substantial additional funds. We will continue to expend significant resources for the foreseeable future in connection with these activities. These expenditures will include costs associated with conducting preclinical studies and clinical trials, obtaining regulatory approvals and manufacturing and supply, as well as marketing and selling any products approved for sale. In addition, other unanticipated costs may arise. Because the outcome of any preclinical study or clinical trial is highly uncertain, we cannot reasonably estimate the actual amounts necessary to successfully complete the development and commercialization of our product candidates or any future product candidates.

paragraphs: 本年度報表為 Form 10-K 申報書，"we," "our," "us," "Annexon" 以及 "the Company" 皆指 Annexon, Inc. 及其合併子公司。Annexon、Annexon, Inc.、Annexon 燈號及其他商標、服務標誌皆為 Annexon, Inc. 所有。本報告包含對本公司商標及其他公司商標的參考。本報告中出現的其他公司商標、服務標誌為其各自所有者所有。本公司並未有意透過使用或展示其他公司商標或服務標誌，暗示與任何其他公司有關係，或獲得其認可或贊助。
本公司為一生物科技公司，致力於發展新一代的標的性免疫治療平台，用以對抗影響全球近 10 百萬人的補體媒介神經發炎疾病。經典補體路徑是身體免疫系統的核心零組件，會啟動強大的發炎 cascade。我們相信透過在經典補體路徑起始點針對 C1q（經典補體路徑的起始分子）進行幹擾，我們的方法可能具有潛力，提供更完整的保護，以對抗補體媒介的身體、腦部及眼疾。

透過我們的專利平台，我們正在識別並釐清經典補體路徑在三個治療領域—自身免疫、神經退化及眼科—中的角色。在進行此過程時，我們正在推動一串產品候選藥物，設計用以阻斷經典補體路徑的早期 cascade 以及所有下游路徑零組件及其組織損害功能。我們的目標是抑制過度或異常的經典補體活動，以減緩或甚至停止疾病進展，同時保留參與清除病原體及受損細胞的凝集素及替代補體路徑的有益免疫功能。基於超過十年的經驗，我們已證明在身體、腦部及眼疾中對目標的強大作用，並在多種疾病中取得臨牀概念驗證。
我們的戰略優先事項包括推進兩個晚期註冊計畫：tanruprubart，朝向我們在格林巴利症候羣（Guillain-Barré Syndrome, GBS）的首次潛在批准，以及 vonaprument，朝向地圖性萎縮（geographic atrophy, GA）的關鍵數據，以及開發 ANX1502，一種新型口服小分子藥物，用於自身免疫疾病。

Tanruprubart 是一種正在進行臨牀研究的標的免疫治療藥物，以單次靜脈注射方式快速抑制 GBS 所導致的嚴重神經發炎與損傷，GBS 是一種急性、罕見、神經肌肉系統緊急疾病，每年全球約影響 150,000 人。目前尚無 FDA 批准的治療 GBS 的療法，且現行標準照護也缺乏顯著有效的證據。在安慰劑對照的第三期臨牀試驗中，約 90% 接受 Tanruprubart 治療的 GBS 患者在第 1 週時改善，且在第 26 週時，超過兩倍的治療患者達到正常健康狀態。Tanruprubart 一直顯示出快速且持續的功能改善，包含成功安慰劑對照的證據概念（POC）及第三期臨牀數據、真實世界證據（RWE）、與現行標準照護治療效果的間接比較數據，以及與現行標準照護的藥物間交互作用安全性數據。由於 GBS 疾病過程突然且嚴重，且美國尚無批准的對照藥物，因此已完成安慰劑對照試驗於東南亞地區。美國與歐洲的開放標籤 FORWARD 試驗仍在進行中，設計用以支持廣泛的 GBS 治療標籤，並進一步擴展 Tanruprubart 在不同地區的應用。

我們於 2026 年 1 月向歐洲藥物管理局（EMA）提交了 Tanruprubart 用於治療 GBS 的上市許可申請（MAA），並持續與 EU 管理機構合作進行 MAA 審查程序。Tanruprubart 已獲得 EMA 的罕見疾病指定。Tanruprubart 也已獲得 FDA 的快速通道與罕見疾病藥物指定，用於治療 GBS。目前進行中的開放標籤美國/歐洲 FORWARD 試驗旨在擴展西方對 Tanruprubart 的經驗，我們預期在 2026 年獲得初步藥代動力學（PK）、藥效動力學（PD）、生物標記物及功能數據，以補充我們對 Tanruprubart 在 GBS 中的完整數據包。在獲得這些數據後，我們計畫與 FDA 協商，
以達成對我們目前及補充數據包與支持 Tanruprubart 在西方患者中普遍適用性的資訊的共識，並於 2026 年提交生物製品許可申請（BLA）。

Vonaprument 是一種正在進行臨牀研究的神經保護劑，用以抑制 C1q 與經典補體 cascade，以治療乾性 AMD 伴隨 GA，這是導致失明的主要原因之一，影響全球超過八百萬人。目前尚無針對 GA 以維持視力的批准療法。Vonaprument 是唯一在 GA 中顯示出顯著視力維持的臨牀研究療法，於最佳矯正視力（BCVA）與低亮度視力（LLVA）評估中顯示出顯著的視力維持，並在正常與低光條件下提供顯著的視力保護，同時也顯著維持中央視網膜感光細胞，這些細胞對視力至關重要。在第二期 ARCHER 試驗中，Vonaprument 也將 15 字母視力喪失的風險降低超過 70%。
2025年7月，我們完成ARCHER II試驗的659名病患入組，此為一項全球性、偽裝控制、雙盲第三期試驗，用於治療GA病患。ARCHER II的主要評估指標為視力的黃金標準，即評估病患在第15個月內任何兩次連續訪問時確認的BCVA ≥15字母喪失的比例。次要評估指標為橢球區，或EZ，喪失，這是光感受器健康與功能的重要解剖學指標。我們預計於2026年第四季公佈初步數據。

我們已建立與FDA及EMA的全球註冊路徑，支持vonaprument有機會成為歐洲與美國首個核准用以保護GA病患視力的治療藥物。單一試驗計畫將根據FDA的兩試驗建議，在美國分析為兩個子試驗。vonaprument為首個且唯一獲得EMA Priority Medicine，或PRIME，指定的治療GA的療法候選藥物，此指定提供早期且主動的支援，以協助開發具重大治療優勢或對無治療選擇的病患有益的潛在藥物。vonaprument亦被EMA選為2025年7月啟動的產品開發協調員試點計畫的參與者，以協助PRIME指定持有者有效進行監管互動，包括加速科學建議、MAA提交準備活動，以及開發計畫期間的臨時查詢。

ANX1502為一種新型口服小分子藥物，可抑制C1s的活化形式，C1s為C1q所攜帶以啟動經典級聯的酵素，我們認為此藥物為首創且具備選擇性上游經典補體抑制的優勢，同時擁有口服給藥的便利性與靈活性。在針對健康志願者設計的Phase 1單劑遞增，或SAD，及多劑遞增，或MAD，臨牀試驗中，用以評估安全性、耐受性、藥動學與藥效動力學，ANX1502在各組中普遍耐受良好，無嚴重不良事件，達到目標的活性藥物濃度，並對補體活動的藥效動力學生物標記顯示支持性影響。我們正在評估ANX1502的腸衣片劑型，用於持續進行的臨牀前概念驗證試驗中，用以治療冷凝集素血癥，或CAD。我們已觀察到在空腹CAD病患中，藥物濃度達到並超過預設目標。劑量仍在進行中，以增進對ANX1502特性的理解，我們預計在2026年試驗完成時提供更新資訊。

Annexon由已故的Ben Barres博士共同創立，他是國家科學院院士、史丹福大學神經生物學系主任，並為補體介導神經退化研究的先驅；以及Arnon Rosenthal博士，一位世界知名的科學家與產業高階主管。我們已組建一支經驗豐富且成就斐然的管理團隊，參與過多項上市藥物的發現、開發、核准與商業化，並長期研究補體路徑與自身免疫及神經退化性疾病。我們的團隊進一步由經驗豐富的科學顧問委員會、董事會及領先的醫療投資者支持，他們與我們共同致力於開發針對身體、腦部與眼疾的神經發炎疾病的疾病修正藥物。
我們擁有全球開發與商業化權，包括透過獨家授權，所有產品候選藥物，這使我們能戰略性地最大化產品組合的價值。我們的專利組合包括針對我們目標免疫療法平台及各產品候選藥物的專利保護。
我們的產品線包含多樣化的藥物候選藥物，旨在解決具有重大未滿足醫療需求的神經發炎疾病，並具備提供首創治療機會的潛力。我們的產品線如下：

除了歷史財務資訊外，下列討論包含向前看的陳述，反映我們的計畫、預估、信念與預期，並涉及風險與不確定性。造成或促成這些差異的因素包括下列所討論之內容，以及其他本年度10-K申報表中之內容，特別是在標題為「特別提醒向前看陳述」與「風險因素」之部分。
我們是一家生物製藥公司，致力於發展新一代的標的免疫治療平台，用以治療影響全球近10百萬人的補體媒介神經發炎疾病。基於超過十年的專業經驗，我們已成功在體內、腦部與眼睛中顯示出強大的標的結合，並在多種疾病中展示臨牀概念驗證。
我們的戰略優先事項包括推進兩個晚期註冊計畫，tanruprubart朝向第一個核准用於吉蘭-巴雷症候羣，或GBS，以及vonaprument朝向地理性視網膜退化，或GA，的重要數據，以及開發ANX1502，一種新型口服小分子藥物，用於自身免疫性疾病。

Tanruprubart是一種正在研究中的標的免疫治療藥物，以單次靜脈注射方式給藥，用以迅速停止GBS的劇烈神經發炎與損傷，GBS是一種急性、罕見、神經肌肉急症，每年影響全球約15萬人。目前尚無經FDA核准的治療方式，且現有標準照護也缺乏有效性證據。在安慰劑對照的第三期臨牀試驗中，約有90%的GBS患者在第1週接受tanruprubart治療後改善，且在第26週時，超過兩倍的治療患者達到正常健康狀態。Tanruprubart已持續顯示出快速且持續的功能改善，並在完整的數據包中表現良好。美國與歐洲的開放標籤FORWARD研究仍在進行中，旨在支持廣泛的標籤，用以治療GBS，並進一步擴展tanruprubart在不同地區的應用。我們持續與適用的歐盟與美國監管機構合作，以推動tanruprubart在全球取得核准。我們於2026年1月向歐洲藥物管理局，或EMA，提交了tanruprubart用於治療GBS的上市許可申請，或MAA。我們計畫於2026年向FDA提交生物製品許可申請，或BLA，用於治療GBS。Tanruprubart已獲得FDA授予快速通道與罕見疾病藥物指定。Tanruprubart也已獲得EMA授予罕見疾病藥物指定。

Vonaprument是一種正在研究中的神經保護劑，用以抑制C1q與經典補體級聯反應，並以玻璃體內注射方式用於GA，一種導致失明的主要原因，影響全球超過八百萬人。目前尚無核准用於GA的治療方式，用以維持視力。Vonaprument是唯一在GA中顯示出顯著視力維持的正在研究中的治療方式，並在最佳校正視力，或BCVA，以及低光度視力，或LLVA，的評估中顯示出顯著的視力喪失保護，並在正常與低光條件下均顯示出顯著的視力維持，以及顯著維持中央視網膜感光細胞，這些細胞對視力至關重要。在第二期ARCHER試驗中，Vonaprument也將15字母視力喪失的風險降低超過70%。

2025年7月，我們完成了ARCHER II試驗的659名患者入組，這是一項全球、安慰劑對照、雙盲的第三期試驗。ARCHER II的主要評估指標是視力的黃金標準，測量在15個月內，兩次連續訪問中確認的BCVA ≥15字母喪失的比例。次要評估指標為EZ喪失，這是感光細胞健康與功能的重要解剖學指標。我們計畫於2026年第四季報告主要數據。我們已建立與FDA及EMA的全球註冊路徑，這支持Vonaprument有潛力成為歐洲與美國首個核准用於GA患者視力保護的治療方式。單一試驗計畫將在美國分析為兩個子試驗，依照FDA的兩試驗建議。Vonaprument是首個且唯一獲得EMA授予優先藥物，或PRIME，指定的GA治療候選藥物，這為開發潛在重大治療優勢或對無治療選擇的患者有益的藥物的開發者提供早期且主動的支援。Vonaprument也獲EMA選為產品開發協調員試點計畫，於2025年7月啟動，以協助PRIME指定持有者高效地進行監管互動，包括加速科學建議、MAA提交準備活動，以及開發過程中的臨時查詢。

ANX1502 是一種新型口服小分子藥物，可抑制 C1s 的活化形式，C1s 是由 C1q 帶載以啟動經典補體級聯反應的酵素，我們認為此藥物為首創類型，具有選擇性上游經典補體抑制的優勢，同時兼具口服給藥的便利性與靈活性。在針對健康志工設計的 Phase 1 單劑遞增與多劑遞增臨牀試驗中，用以評估安全性、耐受性、藥動學與藥效學，ANX1502 在各組別中普遍耐受良好，無嚴重不良事件，達到目標的活化藥物濃度，並對補體活性的藥效學生物指標產生支持性影響。我們正在評估 ANX1502 的腸溶片劑型，用於持續進行的初步臨牀試驗，針對冷凝集素疾病（Cold Agglutinin Disease, CAD）患者。我們已觀察到在空腹 CAD 患者中，藥物濃度達到並超過預設目標。劑量調整仍在進行中，以增進對 ANX1502 的瞭解，我們預計在 2026 年試驗完成後提供更新資訊。

本公司於 2011 年 3 月成立，同年後期開始營運。截至目前為止，我們主要致力於進行研究與開發活動、聘僱人員及籌措資金以支持並擴展這些活動。我們目前尚無任何已核准上市的產品，也尚未從產品銷售中產生任何收入。自成立以來，我們每年均產生淨虧損。本公司 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日的淨虧損分別為 206.7 百萬美元及 138.2 百萬美元。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司累計虧損為 917.4 百萬美元，現金及現金等價物與短期投資為 238.3 百萬美元。
我們的產品候選藥物尚未核准上市銷售。我們尚未從產品候選藥物的銷售中產生任何收入，且在可預見的未來亦不會產生收入，直到我們完成臨牀開發、提交相關監管文件並獲得相關監管機構核准這些產品候選藥物為止。
研究與開發費用佔我們營運費用的很大一部分。研究與開發費用主要為進行產品候選藥物開發所產生的直接與間接成本。
• 與產品候選藥物的發現、臨牀前及臨牀測試相關的外部服務費用；
• 與第三方合同組織、臨牀試驗場地及顧問簽訂的專業服務協議，這些機構代表本公司進行研究與開發活動；

自本公司成立以來，本公司已產生重大營運虧損。本公司截至2025年12月31日及2024年12月31日之淨虧損約為206.7 百萬美元及138.2 百萬美元。截至2025年12月31日，本公司累計虧損為917.4 百萬美元。本公司虧損幾乎全部來自與研究與開發計畫相關之費用，以及與營運相關之總務及行政費用。本公司預期將持續產生虧損，且預期這些虧損將持續至我們開發產品候選藥物、進行臨牀試驗及追求研究與開發活動為止。即使本公司未來達成獲利，亦可能無法維持後續期間之獲利。本公司過去虧損與預期未來虧損，已對股東權益與營運資金產生及將持續產生負面影響。
本公司將需要大量額外資金以達成目標，若無法在需要時以可接受之條件或完全無法取得必要資金，將迫使本公司延遲、限制、減少或終止產品開發計畫、商業化努力或其他營運活動。

自本公司成立以來，本公司已將大量努力與財務資源投入研究與開發活動。產品候選藥物將需要額外臨牀開發，且本公司有意進行額外研究與開發活動以發現與開發新產品候選藥物，包括進行非臨牀研究與臨牀試驗，所有這些均需大量額外資金。本公司將持續在可預見之未來投入大量資源於這些活動。這些支出將包括進行非臨牀研究與臨牀試驗之費用、取得監管核准之費用、製造與供應，以及行銷與銷售任何核准銷售之產品。此外，其他未預期之費用亦可能產生。由於任何非臨牀研究或臨牀試驗之結果極為不確定，本公司無法合理預估完成產品候選藥物或任何未來產品候選藥物之開發與商業化所需之實際金額。
